questions.question: Ratha Jatra, the festival of Chariots of Lord Jagannatha is celebrated every year in ______.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Puri, Odisha**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Origins and Significance:**

 
• **Ratha Jatra,** also known as the **Chariot Festival,** is a significant event in** Hinduism.**
 
• It is dedicated to** Lord Jagannatha, a form of Lord Vishnu,** and his siblings, **Lord Balabhadra and Goddess Subhadra.**
 
• The festival symbolizes **Lord Jagannatha's annual visit to his birthplace, the Gundicha Temple.**

**Location and Time:**

 
• The festival takes place in **Puri, a city in the Indian state of Odisha.**
 
• It is usually held in the month of Ashadha, which falls in June or July according to the **Gregorian calendar.**

**Chariot Construction and Procession:**

 
• Three chariots are constructed for the festival, each representing one of the deities - **Lord Jagannatha, Lord Balabhadra, and Goddess Subhadra.**
 
• These chariots are pulled by devotees in a grand procession from the main Jagannatha temple to the **Gundicha Temple.**

**Rituals and Celebrations: **

 
• The festival lasts for **nine days.**
 
• The deities are bathed and adorned with new clothes and jewelry.
 
• They are then placed on the chariots for the procession.
 
• Upon reaching the Gundicha Temple, they stay there for seven days and then return to the **main temple, marking the end of the festival.**

**Global Recognition:**

 
• While the festival has its roots in Puri, it is now celebrated globally by the **International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) **and other Hindu communities around the world.
 
• The festival is known for its display of devotion and the **vibrant cultural heritage of Odisha.**

• Bathukamma is a vibrant and unique floral festival celebrated predominantly by the women of Telangana, India.
 
• The festival is a nine-day celebration that typically falls during the Hindu month of Ashwina, coinciding with the latter part of the monsoon and the beginning of winter.
 
• Bathukamma literally translates to "Mother Goddess come alive."
 
• The festival is a tribute to the Goddess Gauri, a form of Parvati, and celebrates womanhood, nature, and the spirit of togetherness.
 
• During Bathukamma, womenfolk meticulously arrange seasonal flowers into colorful, conical stacks, representing the Goddess.
 
• These stacks, also called "Bathukammas," are beautifully decorated with various flowers like gunugu, tangedu, chamanti, and others, each chosen for its unique color and fragrance.
 
• In the evenings, women gather in large numbers, carrying their decorated Bathukammas to the village center or temple.
 
• They sing traditional folk songs and dance around the Bathukammas in rhythmic circles, creating a mesmerizing and festive atmosphere.
 
• The songs, known as Bathukamma paatalu, narrate stories of local legends, mythology, and the daily lives of women.
 
• On the final day of the festival, known as Saddula Bathukamma, the Bathukammas are immersed in a nearby water body like a pond or a lake.
 
• Before immersion, a special offering called "saddulu" (cooked rice with sesame seeds or cream) is placed near the Bathukamma.
 
• The immersion signifies the return of the Goddess to her heavenly abode, with prayers for prosperity and well-being.
 
• Bathukamma is not just a religious festival; it is also a cultural expression that showcases the rich traditions and the deep connection of the people with nature.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals marks the birth of Prince Siddhartha Gautama, who founded a religion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddha Purnima**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Buddha Purnima**, also known as Vesak, commemorates the birth, enlightenment, and death (Mahaparinirvana) of Gautama Buddha.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) in the Hindu month of Vaishakha (April-May).
 
• It marks the birth anniversary of **Prince Siddhartha Gautama**, who later became Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism.
 
• Buddha Purnima is observed by Buddhists across the world, especially in countries like India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, and Southeast Asian nations.
 
• The day is significant for Buddhists, as it symbolizes the teachings of Buddha and his path toward liberation from suffering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prince Siddhartha Gautama:**

 
 
• Born in Lumbini (present-day Nepal) in 563 BCE to King Suddhodana and Queen Maya Devi.
 
• Renounced royal life at the age of 29 to seek answers to life's suffering.
 
• Attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree in Bodh Gaya, India, becoming the Buddha ("The Enlightened One").
 
 
 
• **Core Teachings of Buddha:**
 
 
• The Four Noble Truths: Dukkha (suffering), Samudaya (cause of suffering), Nirodha (end of suffering), and Magga (path to cessation of suffering).
 
• The Eightfold Path (Ashtanga Marg): Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, and Right Concentration.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Vesak (Buddha Purnima):**
 
 
• Devotees visit monasteries, offer prayers, and chant Buddhist scriptures.
 
• Acts of kindness and generosity are encouraged, including donations to the needy.
 
• The Bodhi Tree is often adorned with decorations to honor the site of Buddha's enlightenment.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism in the Modern World:**
 
 
• Buddhism is one of the world's major religions, with over 500 million followers globally.
 
• Countries like Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, and Japan are predominantly Buddhist.
 
• The teachings of Buddha emphasize mindfulness, meditation, and ethical living, which remain relevant in contemporary times.
